construct: Osteoblast-lineage cells regulate osteoclast differentiation through RANKL, which binds RANK on osteoclast precursors. Osteoprotegerin (OPG), secreted by osteoblast/stromal cells, binds RANKL as a decoy receptor and prevents RANK activation, thereby suppressing osteoclast formation and bone resorption.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Osteoblast-lineage overexpression of osteoprotegerin suppresses osteoclast maturation by binding RANKL before it can activate RANK on osteoclast precursors.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: M-CSF signaling is also essential for osteoclast precursor biology and is the strongest alternative pathway, but the stem explicitly preserves M-CSF signaling and OPG does not neutralize M-CSF.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only RANKL-RANK is the ligand-receptor interaction directly intercepted by soluble osteoprotegerin.
